item.title: St. Louis Democratic House primary exposes party rifts over Israel
item.description: St. Louis Public Radio hosted one of the first media appearances this year between Rep. Wesley Bell and former Congresswoman Cori Bush. The primary race is a rematch of a race Bush lost last year to Bell.

item.title: Nicaragua's President Ortega says there will be no more elections, extending his rule
item.description: Nicaragua's President Daniel Ortega declares "there won't be any more elections," cementing his grip on power and ending hopes for a democratic vote.

item.title: U.S. reports highest number of measles cases in 35 years
item.description: For the second year in a row, the U.S. has reported a record-breaking number of measles cases. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on Friday said the country has now confirmed 2,318 measles cases -- the highest case count since 1991.

item.title: 15 years later, is the FDA's produce safety overhaul working?
item.description: Fifteen years ago, the FDA overhauled its safety rules for fruits and vegetables, hoping to prevent outbreaks of foodborne illness. How's that system working today?

item.title: Justice Department is offering billions in new grants for police who partner with ICE
item.description: The DOJ is offering state and local police $3 billion to cooperate with ICE on federal immigration enforcement, part of a broader effort to expand the administration's mass deportation campaign.
